A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Vintix and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Existing material can be matched reliably across appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original Vintix experiments across four domains, including inference-time adaptation, parameter variations and held-out tasks, with detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds expert-distillation and reward-masking control experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Continuous Noise Distillation, the Vintix architecture, prediction loss and inference procedure are retained. The added group-identifier explanation clarifies the existing architecture; Appendix C introduces experimental controls, not a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four domains, 87 training tasks, held-out tasks and physical-parameter variations. The additional comparisons and controls reuse MuJoCo and Meta-World; they introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix I add REGENT to the previously JAT-only cross-agent comparison, using published comparator scores. Appendix C additionally evaluates an architecture-matched Expert Distillation model and reward-masked AD, substantially expanding the comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds expert-only training and reward-masking controls evaluated through cold-start inference. Figure 8 reports mean normalized scores, whereas the retained main adaptation plots use IQM. Existing benchmark splits, rollout settings and Vintix's 100-episode comparison protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Sections C.1–C.2 test whether policy-improvement trajectories outperform expert-only demonstrations under the same architecture and whether rewards contribute to adaptation. Figure 8 supplies direct controls for central mechanism claims that v1 lacked. Existing generalization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 removes the explicit 100-trial JAT disclosure and Figure 5's Vintix error bars, while newly tabulating JAT scores with ± values in Tables 11–12. Other 95% confidence-interval displays remain. No increase in independent runs or seeds is documented.

E6.justification: Appendix C newly reports ED scores around 0.80 versus AD scores of 0.97 on MuJoCo and 0.95 on Meta-World, plus poorer reward-masked performance. Appendix I adds task-level REGENT and JAT results, and Figure 5 revises aggregate bars. Existing task-level Vintix tables retain their values; the new mean-based controls do not establish changes to earlier IQM results.

T1.justification: The trajectory and task notation, Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.3's noise-schedule formula are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about continuous noise distillation, cross-domain ICRL, self-correction and limited generalization. The added experiments support existing core claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets the controls as evidence that policy-improvement structure enables self-correction and reward feedback is essential for effective inference-time improvement. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning unseen-task generalization remain.

D1.justification: Section 2.3.1 clarifies that group identifiers concern shared dimensions and channel semantics. Appendix C documents architecture/loss matching and reward removal for its controls. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, dataset metadata and the promised code-release information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds a Sequence Modeling in RL discussion and five references covering Decision Transformer, Janner et al.'s sequence model, Online Decision Transformer, Decision Mamba and Reinformer. This extends positioning within an existing research lineage. REGENT was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. Local revisions clarify group identifiers, update the comparison discussion, expand related work and introduce Appendices C and I. Author spelling, affiliations, publication information and several typographical details also change.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redrawn for three comparators, Figure 8 and Tables 11–12 are added, and Figure 4 is relocated. The hyperparameter table is reformatted and captioned. Existing appendix plots and numerical tables are retained with renumbering and limited repositioning.

improvement.justification: v1 supported AD's advantage mainly through comparison with JAT, leaving architecture differences intertwined with the training approach. v2's architecture-matched ED control and reward-masking experiment directly strengthen evidence for the paper's central explanations; REGENT and task-level comparisons broaden scrutiny. These address important evidential gaps, although the new controls' training budgets and run details remain sparse and Figure 5 loses uncertainty bars.
